fjk_001: You can recognise it by its huge trunk, twelve metres round, towering over the shrine yard. It stands in the grounds of Suwa Shrine, in Shoji.
fjk_002: You can recognise it lying flat on the ground, snapped near its base, with new shoots and fruit growing straight from the fallen trunk. It stands on the grounds of Jotakuji Temple.
fjk_003: You can recognise it by the single high branch, eight to ten metres up, that alone among the tree bears seeds. It stands on the grounds of Yamajinja shrine, in Kamiyagisawa.
fjk_004: You can recognise it by its trunk, thicker at the base than at chest height, with comparatively few of the milky growths older ginkgos often carry. It stands between the guardian gate and main hall of Hongokuji Temple.
fjk_005: You can recognise it by the support structure holding up its storm-damaged vine, near a companion vine tangled into a maple. It stands in the grounds of Yama-jinja shrine, in Kamikureji.
